signature: SUBROUTINE DLAEBZ( IJOB, NITMAX, N, MMAX, MINP, NBMIN, ABSTOL,

params.name: ijob
params.reference:
Specifies what is to be done:

-   `= 1`: Compute `NAB` for the initial intervals.
-   `= 2`: Perform bisection iteration to find eigenvalues of T.
-   `= 3`: Perform bisection iteration to invert `N(w)`, i.e., to find a point which has a specified number of eigenvalues of T to its left. Other values will cause DLAEBZ to return with `INFO=-1`.

params.name: nitmax
params.reference: The maximum number of "levels" of bisection to be performed, i.e., an interval of width W will not be made smaller than 2^$(-\mathrm{NITMAX}) \, W$. If not all intervals have converged after `NITMAX` iterations, then `INFO` is set to the number of non-converged intervals.

params.name: N
params.reference: The dimension n of the tridiagonal matrix T. It must be at least 1.

params.name: mmax
params.reference: The maximum number of intervals. If more than `MMAX` intervals are generated, then DLAEBZ will quit with $\mathrm{INFO}=\mathrm{MMAX}+1$.

params.name: minp
params.reference: The initial number of intervals. It may not be greater than `MMAX`.

params.name: nbmin
params.reference: The smallest number of intervals that should be processed using a vector loop. If zero, then only the scalar loop will be used.

params.name: abstol
params.reference: The minimum (absolute) width of an interval. When an interval is narrower than `ABSTOL`, or than `RELTOL` times the larger (in magnitude) endpoint, then it is considered to be sufficiently small, i.e., converged. This must be at least zero.

params.name: reltol
params.reference: The minimum relative width of an interval. When an interval is narrower than `ABSTOL`, or than `RELTOL` times the larger (in magnitude) endpoint, then it is considered to be sufficiently small, i.e., converged. Note: this should always be at least radix\*machine $\epsilon$.

params.name: pivmin
params.reference: The minimum absolute value of a "pivot" in the Sturm sequence loop. This must be at least max \|$e(j)^2$\|\*safe\_min and at least safe\_min, where safe\_min is at least the smallest number that can divide one without overflow.

params.name: d
params.reference: The diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T.

params.name: e
params.reference: The offdiagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T in positions 1 through N-1. `E(N)` is arbitrary.

params.name: E2
params.reference: The squares of the offdiagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T. `E2(N)` is ignored.

params.name: NVAL
params.reference: If `IJOB=1` or 2, not referenced. If `IJOB=3`, the desired values of `N(w)`. The elements of `NVAL` will be reordered to correspond with the intervals in `AB`. Thus, `NVAL(j)` on output will not, in general be the same as `NVAL(j)` on input, but it will correspond with the interval (`AB(j,1)`,`AB(j,2)`\] on output.

params.name: AB
params.reference: The endpoints of the intervals. `AB(j,1)` is a(j), the left endpoint of the j-th interval, and `AB(j,2)` is b(j), the right endpoint of the j-th interval. The input intervals will, in general, be modified, split, and reordered by the calculation.

params.name: c
params.reference: If `IJOB=1`, ignored. If `IJOB=2`, workspace. If `IJOB=3`, then on input `C(j)` should be initialized to the first search point in the binary search.

params.name: mout
params.reference: If `IJOB=1`, the number of eigenvalues in the intervals. If `IJOB=2` or 3, the number of intervals output. If `IJOB=3`, `MOUT` will equal `MINP`.

params.name: NAB
params.reference:
If `IJOB=1`, then on output `NAB(i,j)` will be set to `N(AB(i,j))`. If `IJOB=2`, then on input, `NAB(i,j)` should be set. It must

-   satisfy the condition:
-   $N(\mathrm{AB}(i,1)) \le \mathrm{NAB}(i,1) \le \mathrm{NAB}(i,2) \le N(\mathrm{AB}(i,2))$,
-   which means that in interval i only eigenvalues
-   `NAB(i,1)`+1,...,`NAB(i,2)` will be considered. Usually,
-   `NAB(i,j)=N(AB(i,j))`, from a previous call to DLAEBZ with
-   `IJOB=1`.
-   On output, `NAB(i,j)` will contain
-   max(na(k),min(nb(k),`N(AB(i,j))`)), where k is the index of
-   the input interval that the output interval
-   (`AB(j,1)`,`AB(j,2)`\] came from, and na(k) and nb(k) are the
-   the input values of `NAB(k,1)` and `NAB(k,2)`.

If `IJOB=3`, then on output, `NAB(i,j)` contains `N(AB(i,j))`,

-   unless $N(w) > \mathrm{NVAL}(i)$ for all search points w , in which
-   case `NAB(i,1)` will not be modified, i.e., the output
-   value will be the same as the input value (modulo
-   reorderings -- see `NVAL` and `AB`), or unless $N(w) < \mathrm{NVAL}(i)$
-   for all search points w , in which case `NAB(i,2)` will
-   not be modified. Normally, `NAB` should be set to some
-   distinctive value(s) before DLAEBZ is called.

params.name: WORK
params.reference: Workspace.

params.name: IWORK
params.reference: Workspace.

params.name: info
params.reference: -   `= 0`: All intervals converged. = 1--`MMAX`: The last `INFO` intervals did not converge. = `MMAX`+1:  More than `MMAX` intervals were generated.
